column2: The control with the lower measured delay changed 2 times across the sweep (signal at 2, roundabout at 1 of 8 points, 4 tie(s), 1 inconclusive); there is no single crossover and no consistent direction. Each point is one random traffic pattern, so a difference here may be chance; only the repeated-seed validation tests that. Delay: signal mean 31.91 s, roundabout mean 16.4 s over 5 random traffic patterns; the difference is statistically supported at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.0, Cohen's d = 6.016), with the lower mean at the roundabout. Vehicles served: signal mean 45.8 veh, roundabout mean 51.2 veh over 5 random traffic patterns; not statistically supported at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.0681, Cohen's d = -1.385): this study cannot distinguish the controls on this metric, which is not the same as showing they are equal. Average queue: signal mean 1.55 veh, roundabout mean 0.16 veh over 5 random traffic patterns; the difference is statistically supported at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.0001, Cohen's d = 8.083), with the lower mean at the roundabout.
